note: Existing upstream constructs: inventory, not endorsement of result caching. Changes require explicit review. In-run memoisation/interning is allowed; persisted intermediates and cross-run reuse are not.

review.compilers/shared/cx86_p1.sov::scutr s st: word_id() memoises its last (s -> intern kid) pair in wid_last_s/wid_last_r. Both globals start at 0 in every fresh process. Pure in-run reuse of a pure function; no file I/O, no sidecar, no cross-run or cross-edit state.
review.compilers/shared/cx86_p4.sov::try_stmt_i: ml_collect_cached(bf) memoises ml_collect() results per body pointer in process-local lists (mlc_fi/mlc_txt/mlc_m/...), allocated lazily inside the run. No persistence, no translation-result reuse across runs.
review.compilers/shared/cx86_p7.sov::try_scaled: ik_cached(nm) compares a call-name slice pointer with ik_nm_ptr and returns ik_nm_kid on a hit; the cut arena is append-only so pointer identity is exact. Single-run interning shortcut, no file I/O, no sidecar.
review.compilers/shared/cx86_p1.sov::word_id s: The wid_last_s/wid_last_r last-result pair itself: two globals initialised to 0 in the data section, written and read only inside word_id() during one compile. No persistence of any kind.
review.compilers/shared/cx86_p1.sov::ik_cached: Definition site of the in-run interning shortcut described above. Compares ik_nm_ptr, falls back to intern_kid(); no file I/O, no sidecar literals.
review.compilers/shared/cx86_p4.sov::ml_collect: Definition site of the per-body ml_collect() memo described above. C.4/C.6 replaced its linear scan over mlc_fi with a direct-indexed O(1) table (mlc_tab[bf] = ci+1, 0 = absent) plus mlc_tab_ensure() doubling allocator. It is still the SAME pure in-run memo: one entry per body, appended only on a miss, hit restores the same mq_* globals. mlc_tab/mlc_tn are globals initialised to 0 in every fresh process and reset to 0 by build_inl_set(); the table is a heap array allocated inside the current run. No file I/O, no sidecar, no persisted intermediate, no prefix replay, no cross-run or cross-edit reuse of a translation result.
review.compilers/shared/cx86_p6.sov::try_mem na: Calls ik_cached(name) for the same single-run interning shortcut; the block contains no file I/O and no sidecar literals.
